title: The 3AM Warehouse
venue: Concrete warehouse, Berlin. One room, no windows, fog to the knees.
crowd: 400 people, six hours in. The floor is locked but starting to drift.
situation: You have the room. Now take them deeper without losing a single one. The previous DJ left you at 128 BPM and slightly too bright.

title: The Wedding, 10:15 PM
venue: Function hall. Parquet floor, fairy lights, an open bar that has been open a while.
crowd: 120 guests aged 8 to 80. Three generations, one floor.
situation: Dinner is cleared and the floor is half full. Nobody can be left standing at the edge. You need the grandmother and the groomsmen dancing to the same record.

title: Rooftop, Golden Hour
venue: Eighth-floor rooftop. Low sun, warm concrete, a city going orange.
crowd: 80 people arriving with first drinks. Nobody is dancing yet.
situation: Nobody should be dancing yet. Your job is the next four hours, not the next four minutes. Build a room people do not want to leave.

title: The Last 30 Minutes
venue: Small club, lights already coming up at the edges.
crowd: 40 people left. Every one of them chose to still be here.
situation: This is the closing set. No more peaks. Send them out into the morning feeling something they did not walk in with.

title: Main Stage, Peak
venue: Festival main stage. Full rig, CO2 jets, a horizon of people.
crowd: 15,000 people, phones already up, waiting to be detonated.
situation: This is your peak-time slot. Maximum energy, zero subtlety permitted. Every track must be legible to someone 200 metres back who is not a dance music fan.

title: The Basement, 1AM
venue: House party basement. One speaker clipping, low ceiling, condensation on the walls.
crowd: 45 people, sweaty, close friends and their friends.
situation: No booth, no monitors, someone is standing on the sofa. Everyone needs to know the words to something. Nostalgia is a weapon here, but cheap nostalgia will empty the room.
